newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end choppy day higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end choppy day higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished higher but in the lower portion of daily ranges after a choppy session.

Futures rallied sharply in morning dealings on strength linked in part to an advance in the bond market. Weaker than expected February U.S. producer price data bolstered the debt market as the data tempered concerns that the Federal Reserve would move quickly to raise interest rates.
"The numbers came out this morning and the market thought maybe there wasn't as much reason to tighten," said Jay Hohmann, head futures trader at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette.
However, traders were wary of the advance, also attributing it to a technical bounce after the steep fall yesterday.

The June S&P 500 contract, which became the lead contract this week ahead of the expiration of March at the end of next week, broke above resistance at 803.50 on the early advance, which fueled gains.

When the bond market failed to advance further and moved into a sideways trading pattern, selling emerged in index futures which pared gains, at one point late in the afternoon sending the June contract to near unchanged levels for the day.
In the longer-term outlook, Thursday's steep decline did little to damage the technical outlook, Hohmann said.
"The long-term uptrend is still intact. We could have dropped 300 to 400 in the Dow and still not done any damage to the long-term uptrend," he said. The Dow fell 160 points Thursday.
Nikkei 225 stock index futures also posted sizable gains and ended in the upper portion of daily ranges following smaller gains in the spot index overnight.

At settlement, June S&P 500s were up 5.05 points at 803.00, Nasdaq 100s eased 0.25 to 850.75, Russell 2000s rose 1.15 point to 364.40, Value Line futures were up 4.70 points to 723.20, Nikkei 225 index futures gained 320.0 to 17,950.0 and Midcap 400s were up 2.30 point to 268.80.
